paragraphs: While Swamiji was in New York, he used to watch Irish immigrants arriving. They came in worn out and beaten down, having lost everything at home. All they owned was a bundle of rags tied to the end of a stick. Their steps were nervous and their eyes were full of fear.
Six months later, Swamiji said, the same man looked completely different. He walked upright, dressed differently, and the fear had vanished from his eyes and his walk. What had changed?

Swamiji's explanation came from Vedanta. Back home, the man had lived surrounded by contempt. Everything around him seemed to tell him the same thing: you have no hope, you were born a slave and you will stay one. He had heard it from birth, so he believed it. He had practically hypnotised himself into thinking he was small, and the divine power within him shrank and hid.

Then he landed in America, and everywhere he heard the opposite message. You are a man, just like us. People like you and me have built everything; we can do anything. Have courage! He lifted his head, saw that it was true, and the sleeping divinity inside him woke up. It was as if nature itself were calling out to him: "Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached."
learn: What you hear about yourself every day, from family, society or your own inner voice, quietly shapes who you become. Choose surroundings and thoughts that tell you that you can. And be that voice of courage for someone else.
